### First Impressions
Author: Dennis Fisher
Site: Our Daily Bread
URL: https://military.odb.org/first-impressions/
Passage: 1 Samuel 16:7
Points:
- People routinely form hasty opinions about others based strictly on external appearances.
- Samuel initially made the same mistake by judging Jesse's oldest son by physical stature.
- God bypassed the impressive older brothers to choose David, who looked least like a king.
- Human beings look at visible traits, but the Lord evaluates the unseen condition of the heart.
- Believers must rely on God to view people through His eyes rather than snap judgments.

### Appearances Can Be Deceiving
Author: Laura MacCorkle
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/appearances-can-be-deceiving-crosswalk-the-devotional-aug-19-2010-11635560.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 16:7
Points:
- God frequently chooses individuals whom human standards would overlook or deem unqualified.
- Samuel expected Eliab to be the chosen king because of his height and appearance.
- The Lord directed Samuel to David, an inexperienced young shepherd, and anointed him for service.
- Believers often limit themselves by focusing on personal shortcomings, lack of eloquence, or status.
- Faith requires evaluating yourself and others through God's perspective rather than cultural metrics.

### Power Point - July 24, 2006
Author: PowerPoint Ministries
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/powerpoint/power-point-july-24-2006-1408849.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 16:7
Points:
- Jesse's older sons formed an impressive group outwardly, but their hearts were not yielded to God.
- David was considered the least likely candidate by human metrics while faithfully tending sheep.
- The Lord prioritizes inner devotion and humility over outward charm, intellect, or financial wealth.
- Quiet faithfulness in small tasks positions a believer to be entrusted with greater responsibility.
- God can elevate anyone into impactful kingdom service when their heart is wholly dedicated to Him.

### Deconstructing David
Author: Ryan Duncan
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/deconstructing-david-crosswalk-the-devotional-march-19-2012.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 16:7
Points:
- God selected David because of his heart rather than outward perfection or invulnerability.
- Being a person after God's heart did not protect David from suffering, conflict, or severe failure.
- Christian discipleship does not ensure worldly ease or freedom from adversity.
- David's defining spiritual quality was that he consistently turned back to God in times of crisis.
- What God desires most is a heart that remains committed and dependent on Him through life's trials.
